verdict.root_cause: The only measured failure is on checkoutservice: its own span error ratio rose from ~0.04% baseline to ~11% mean with peaks near 67%, first breaching threshold at 12:02:30 — about 80 minutes before the 13:24:15 paymentservice alert [tr_50d18f22666d]. paymentservice shows no failure of its own: logs covering 13:24:07 onward contain only info-level charge/complete pairs with no errors or downstream timeouts, continuing to the window edge [tr_5129518395da], and checkout's own logs show payment authorizations succeeding with distinct transaction IDs at both window ends [tr_fc84f1f5a321]. The OTLP traces endpoint toggle five minutes before onset does not fit as the mechanism: checkout was already failing 76 minutes earlier, three identical set/revert cycles the same day produced no comparable onset, and the change only touches telemetry export [tr_43a6e07ebaf1]. The failing mechanism is an intermittent partial error condition on checkoutservice's outbound path that these dispatches did not localize — the wide spread and zero minimum rule out a total dependency outage [tr_50d18f22666d], and the third blast-radius service plus two unmeasured edges were never queried.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent sources exonerate paymentservice: its own logs show only successful charges across the covered span [tr_5129518395da], and checkoutservice's logs corroborate that payment calls returned transaction IDs successfully [tr_fc84f1f5a321]. The measured errors are recorded on checkoutservice's own calls_total series, so the failure is observable at the checkout layer [tr_50d18f22666d]. Timing demotes the change record: first breach 12:02:30 versus the endpoint edit at 13:18:22, and the same toggle applied and reverted three times earlier caused no equivalent onset [tr_43a6e07ebaf1]. paymentservice metrics were absent in both incident and baseline windows, an instrumentation gap predating the event, so they neither support nor refute anything [tr_95a053e1c0b1]. Nothing in the evidence names which downstream call or resource is producing checkout's intermittent errors, so the class stays unknown rather than being pinned to the nearest change.
open_questions: Which downstream call inside checkoutservice's PlaceOrder path carries the error spans? The two unmeasured edges and the third blast-radius service were never queried.
What happened at the 12:02:30 and 12:38:30 change points — no change record was pulled for checkoutservice or its dependencies.
Both log queries dropped the 12:54–13:24 middle, so the actual error lines at onset were never observed; and no saturation or latency metrics exist for either service.

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream dependency of checkoutservice (e.g. the Kafka write, email, or currency path) became intermittently slow or failing, and checkout's errors are waits timing out.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and consistent with the intermittent spread [tr_50d18f22666d], but no latency metric or error log from any downstream was ever collected, so the wait itself is unevidenced.

alternatives.root_cause: The OTLP traces endpoint pointed at an unreachable loopback collector caused exporter blocking on paymentservice, degrading calls checkout makes to it.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout was breaching threshold 76 minutes before the edit landed, and three prior applications of the identical toggle produced no comparable onset [tr_50d18f22666d, tr_43a6e07ebaf1]; payment charges also complete normally after it [tr_5129518395da].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric is expected. The condition to keep watching is the checkoutservice span error ratio (sum by(service_name)(rate(calls_total{service_name="checkoutservice",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) / same without the status filter), which sat at ~11% mean with peaks near 0.67 and a minimum of 0 across the window [tr_50d18f22666d]. It should be re-queried alongside a per-downstream-edge breakdown and a change_history pull for checkoutservice covering 12:02:30 and 12:38:30 before any remediation is attempted.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a change record for checkoutservice or one of its unqueried downstream edges turns up dated at or just before 12:02:30 — that would name a concrete config or image change and would satisfy revert_config or rollback_image preconditions on a service that is actually failing. It is also wrong if a log query covering the dropped 12:54–13:24 middle shows error lines naming a single downstream call, localizing the mechanism. Note the counter-risk of waiting: checkoutservice logs and the metric window both show clean successful PlaceOrder cycles at the window edge [tr_fc84f1f5a321], so the failing condition may be intermittent and unobserved rather than resolved; absence of errors in a truncated tail is not proof of recovery.
proposal.risk: The risk of acting here is concrete and is why I am not. The only action whose preconditions are literally met is revert_config on paymentservice — a prior config is recorded and the OTLP traces endpoint toggle sits inside the window [tr_43a6e07ebaf1]. But paymentservice is not the failing service: its logs show only info-level charge/complete pairs through the window edge with no errors or downstream timeouts [tr_5129518395da], and checkout's error ratio was already breaching threshold 76 minutes before that toggle [tr_50d18f22666d]. Reverting it would recreate a healthy container, drop in-flight charges during the recreate, and produce no observable improvement in checkout's error ratio — which would then be misread as evidence the diagnosis was correct-but-insufficient rather than simply wrong. rollback_image fails its precondition outright: no deploy or image change appears anywhere in the record [tr_43a6e07ebaf1]. restart_service fails its precondition too: nothing points at process state — no crash, no restart banner, Kafka offsets advance without reset [tr_fc84f1f5a321]. Restarting checkoutservice would discard its cache and reset the very intermittent condition we have not yet localized, destroying the evidence needed to find it.
proposal.blast_radius: No one, because nothing changes. For contrast, had I proposed the available action: revert_config on paymentservice recreates its container, and checkoutservice — its caller in this graph — sees connection resets during the recreate, which would push checkout's already-elevated error ratio higher and be indistinguishable from the fault under investigation. frontend, downstream of checkoutservice, would see that as failed orders. A restart of checkoutservice would be seen by frontend directly and would interrupt the PlaceOrder path for every user in flight.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single critical alert on paymentservice, a service in the checkout path, is not something to dismiss and no open incident covers it. Nothing in the alert set points to a specific cause yet.
